subject.title: acp: assistant text corrupted when Gateway revises in-progress output (non-append revision mis-sliced)

question: How should the ACP bridge represent Gateway `replace=true` revisions when standard ACP chunks are append-oriented and already-emitted text may not be retractable?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the durable fix depends on the product/protocol choice for replacement rendering across ACP clients rather than only on changing the slice arithmetic.

options.title: Choose final-correct conservative mapping
options.body: Buffer, restart message identity, or otherwise avoid unretractable provisional output so the final ACP-visible answer is correct across standard clients; this is the recommended direction before automation fixes code.

options.title: Adopt a client-specific replace extension
options.body: Use ACP metadata or client capability behavior only if maintainers are willing to document fallback behavior for clients that ignore it.

options.title: Accept new-message fallback
options.body: Emit replacement snapshots as a new ACP message/messageId and accept that some clients may show both stale and corrected text.

recommendation.title: Choose final-correct conservative mapping
recommendation.body: Buffer, restart message identity, or otherwise avoid unretractable provisional output so the final ACP-visible answer is correct across standard clients; this is the recommended direction before automation fixes code.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the ACP bridge and are the best-routed owner for the cross-protocol behavior choice.
